jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.


THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own a critical domain within MarianaOS. This is a single posting because we recruit for the strongest PMs first and then place them where the fit is best. Through the interview process, we’ll figure out together which part of the system is the right match for your background and instincts.

The scope of what we can touch is enormous. Mining is the last major industrial sector that hasn’t been rebuilt with modern software. The opportunity set isn’t a feature gap on an existing product — it’s entire workflows and systems that don’t exist yet. The problem space spans micron-scale chemistry to kilometer-scale infrastructure.

Ship a feature and you can watch the needle move — recovery rates, reagent consumption, construction timelines, equipment uptime. These aren’t proxy metrics. They’re the actual physics of making metal.




THE PLATFORM: MARIANAOS

MarianaOS is the digital nervous system for mineral projects. It spans the full lifecycle — from capital project execution through autonomous operations. The four domains we are staffing for right now are:

 - PlantOS

Our autonomy platform for mineral processing — lithium refining, SX-EW, flotation, copper recycling and beyond. It uses the same reinforcement learning toolkit powering self-driving vehicles and humanoid robots, except we’re using it for autonomous control of minerals refining circuits.

 - MineOS

Integrates geologic block models, short and long-range mine plans, fleet management systems, and industrial control systems into a single optimization layer. We’re accelerating autonomous fleet deployment and building an accurate digital twin of the site to maximize the lifetime value of the mine.

 - CapitalProjectOS

The integrated operating system that lets Mariana build in half the time, at half the cost — and deliver 10+ projects over the next decade. Fragmented data and spreadsheet-driven coordination are replaced by a unified environment for project deliverables, data and workflows which drives visibility, traceability, rapid decision-making and AI-driven execution.

 - AssetOS

Everything we do at Mariana involves tracking and maintaining physical assets across their lifecycle. The assets we design in CapitalProjectOS, can only be used to their full potential by mine and plantOS if we can keep them in service. That’s where AssetOS fits, this OS supports a world-class maintenance function that turns every PM into an F1-style pit stop.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own a product domain end-to-end — from uncovering the right problems and setting the strategy and roadmap through shipping software that runs in real operations where consequences are physical and feedback is immediate

 - Define what to build by analyzing performance data and talking to domain experts — including figuring out what metrics and instrumentation need to exist in the first place

 - Spend meaningful time at construction sites, processing facilities, and mines to understand how work actually happens — prioritization comes from deep operational knowledge, not market research

 - Work at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI — translating what models can do into what operators will trust, and what robotics can deliver into what sites need

 - Drive clarity in ambiguous situations: break down complex problems, define scope, make tradeoffs explicit, and keep teams focused on what matters most

 - Help build the PM function — this is a small, early PM team where you’ll help establish how we work, how we prioritize, and how we develop PMs behind you
   
   


WHO THRIVES HERE

We’ve seen two profiles excel in this kind of environment. You likely see yourself in one of these:

 - The AI-Forward PM
   
   You’ve worked with ML and AI in production — agents, reinforcement learning, process control, optimization. You know how to bridge the gap between what a model can do and what an end user will actually trust. You’ve translated research into shipped products in high-stakes environments.

 - The Autonomy-Forward PM
   
   You’ve shipped products where hardware and software meet and where software failure has physical consequences. You think in fleet coordination, sensor fusion, and operational reliability. You may have started as an engineer and moved into product because you wanted to own the outcome, not just the component.

 - Technical Generalist
   
   You have strong PM fundamentals, are technically deep and have worked in complex, data intensive environments. You operate well in high ambiguity environments and earned trust of engineers. You don’t start on day one with all the domain expertise needed, but rapid learn and soon own outcomes.

 - Don’t fit neatly into one of these?

We’re also drawn to people with strong PM fundamentals who’ve operated in complex, high-ambiguity environments — or people from industrial backgrounds (manufacturing, energy, construction, logistics) who have genuine product instincts even if “PM” has never been in your title. 




DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Must Have

 - 7+ years of experience in product management, ideally with meaningful time in environments where software intersects with physical systems, industrial operations, or safety-critical applications.  

 - Demonstrated ability to understand users and their problems, prioritize systematically, set clear metrics and deliver products which deliver impact at scale. 

 - Clear and concise communicator; you connect across a huge range of technical literacy from PhD engineers and scientists to field operators with no software background 

 - Demonstrated ability to go deep on technical domains and build credibility with engineers. 

 - Experience leading cross-functional teams through ambiguous, complex projects with competing constraints 

 - Intellectual curiosity.  You want to understand how the domain works, not treat it as a black box 

 - Experimentation and growth mindset / desire and ability to learn.  Software development and product management has and will continue to change; you are excited to apply the latest and greatest technology and techniques to improve Mariana and the product management team. 

 - High agency.  You own the outcome. 

 

Nice to Have

 - Experience with autonomous systems, robotics, or fleet-scale operations

 - Has been part of a team delivering capital projects of meaningful scale as part of engineering, procurement, project management, construction or other functions

 - Hands-on work with ML-powered products — especially RL, process control, or optimization in production settings

 - Background in industrial software, digital twin systems, or process automation

 - Track record of digital transformation work in traditional industries

 - An engineering or technical degree (not required, but the instincts it builds are valued)
   
   


WHY THIS ROLE

Most senior PM roles are narrowly scoped — you own one product, one feature set, one customer segment. This role is different.

At Mariana, you don’t need to validate product-market fit because we are the market. If you identify a real problem and build a real solution, adoption is a conversation, not a sales cycle. The constraint is building the right thing, not convincing someone to buy it.

The number and diversity of problems is unusual: you might work across agentic LLM systems for engineering workflows, RL-based process control, and autonomous fleet optimization in the same quarter.

This is not SaaS. This is software that runs mines and refineries. If you’re a strong PM looking for something more substantive than another enterprise software product, we’d love to talk.




WHAT IT’S LIKE TO WORK HERE

Things move fast. The distance between “we should build this” and “it’s running in a real facility” is short — and you’ll feel that pace. You’ll work with an unusually diverse set of collaborators: geologists, metallurgists, chemical engineers, construction managers, plant operators, ML engineers, and software developers. There’s no translation layer between you and the domain experts. They’re your direct collaborators.


OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Share Your Legos. We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.



Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Engineering & Construction
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the Engineering and Super domains of CapitalProjectOS (CPOS), the operating system for how Mariana designs, plans, and builds capital projects. CPOS is organized around four components ( MarianaEngineer (design), MarianaGSM (procurement), MarianaSuper (construction), and MarianaPM (planning and monitoring)) and this role owns two of them end-to-end: MarianaEngineer, the centralized system for design basis, process and engineering data, and 3D models; and MarianaSuper, the real-time command center for construction execution and plan-versus-actual tracking in the field.

You will be the single accountable owner for product strategy, roadmap, and execution across engineering and construction, working alongside PMs who own procurement (GSM) and planning/knowledge (PM) within the same CPOS team. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience in capital project engineering or construction/field execution and is energized by the challenge of embedding AI into workflows that engineers and superintendents depend on every day.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the product vision, roadmap, and prioritization for MarianaEngineer and MarianaSuper, including agentic tooling such as engineering automation, reality capture, and plan-versus-actual intelligence.

 - Serve as the primary domain expert translating capital project engineering and construction workflows into software requirements. You will act as the the bridge between project engineers, superintendents, project controls, software engineering, and executive stakeholders.

 - Embed directly with engineering and field teams to understand how design and construction work actually happens, anticipate edge cases, and distinguish true product requirements from one-off user preferences or process gaps.

 - Write clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and business rules; build and test prototypes to hone in on valuable products as quickly as possible.

 - Build a structured user engagement model (discovery sessions, workflow reviews, sprint reviews, UAT, and adoption check-ins) that makes users accountable for feedback, testing, and adoption.

 - Develop rollout plans, training materials, adoption metrics, and feedback loops; track adoption barriers and work with engineering and construction leaders to resolve them.

 - Define and track success metrics: modeling and design turnaround time, C4 and reality-capture adoption, plan-versus-actual accuracy, cycle time, and downstream project outcomes (schedule, cost, safety).

 - Participate in sprint planning, backlog grooming, and retrospectives; maintain a well-prioritized backlog.

 - Create visibility into what is being built, why it matters, and how it is performing.

 - Help build the PM function at an AI company. This is a small, early team where you'll help establish how we work and develop PMs behind you at a company at the cutting edge of developing and adopting AI.
   
   


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Must Have

 - 5+ years of experience in capital project engineering (process, mechanical, or EPC design) and/or construction or field execution (superintendent, construction management, project controls).

 - Strong understanding of the capital project lifecycle including design basis, engineering deliverables, procurement handoff, construction execution, and commissioning.

 - Ability to go deep on engineering and construction workflows and earn credibility with domain experts by understanding how the work actually happens.

 - Strong product judgment: ruthless prioritization, focus on highest-leverage work, resistance to building everything at once.

 - Ability to translate complex operational workflows into clear requirements, priorities, and product decisions, and to lead cross-functional teams through ambiguous, complex projects with competing stakeholder priorities.

 - Genuine interest in AI-powered tooling. You know how to translate model capabilities into products that engineers and superintendents will trust and adopt, and you enjoy staying current on the cutting edge of AI advancements.

 - Strong communication skills across a wide range of organizational contexts, from field superintendents and engineers to executives.

Nice to Have

 - Direct experience with engineering software (P&ID, 3D/plant design, datasheet or equipment-sizing tools) or construction management software (scheduling, QA/QC, reality capture, command-center platforms).

 - Experience shipping AI-powered enterprise tools: agentic engineering workflows, document intelligence, or process co-pilots.

 - Track record of digital transformation in capital-intensive industries — mining, energy, construction, or manufacturing.

 - Prior product management experience, or genuine excitement to move into product management from an engineering or construction background.

 - AI-forward projects outside of work.
   
   


WHY THIS ROLE

At Mariana, you don't need to validate product-market fit because we are the market. If you identify a real problem and build a real solution, adoption is a conversation, not a sales cycle.

MarianaEngineer and MarianaSuper are the platforms that determine whether Mariana's designs move from design basis to 3D model without drifting out of sync, and whether the field catches a schedule or quality problem in real time instead of in a monthly report. The engineering tools you build set the authoritative source of truth for every project. The command center you build is what a superintendent looks at every morning to run the site.

If you want to own something end-to-end, build software with immediate operational impact, and help shape what a modern industrial company looks like from the inside out — we'd love to talk.


OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!

jobs.title: Sr./Staff Technical Program Manager - Copper
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

The Role

We are hiring Technical Program Managers to own the planning, coordination, and execution of capital projects in Mariana’s portfolio, from idea, to development, through construction and handover to operations.

In this role, you are the single owner of a program. Including scope definition, schedule, budget, and risk register. You coordinate between process development, process engineering, detailed engineering, procurement, construction, business development, and finance. You will build and maintain the execution plan, develop the plan to keep the program the moving and communicate progress, surface risks and decisions before they turn into schedule impacts, and drive them to closure. You will run all of this inside Mariana’s Capital Project OS, the software tools that automate and standardize how we plan, track, and execute programs. You will ensure standardization in execution approaches in the program and provide feedback on Capital Project OS to the software and product management teams to continuously improve the tool.



What You’ll Do

 - Own end-to-end delivery of an assigned capital program—scope, schedule, budget, and risk—from development through construction and handover to operations

 - Build and maintain the integrated program schedule, tracking critical path, interdependencies, long-lead items, and resource needs

 - Own the program budget and cost forecast, partnering with project controls and finance on estimates, commitments, variances, and change control

 - Manage interfaces across process development, process engineering, detailed engineering, procurement, construction, business development, and finance so decisions move quickly and nothing falls between disciplines

 - Run the program cadence and checkpoints. Execution planning, design reviews, status meetings, and readiness gates

 - Surface risks and open decisions early, quantify their schedule and cost impact, drive them to closure, and escalate with a recommendations

 - Produce program reporting and dashboards that give leadership a view of status, critical path, risks, and trade-offs

 - Manage engineering partners, vendors, and contractors against scope, deliverable schedules, and quality expectations

 - Run your program inside Mariana’s Capital Project OS, drive consistent adoption across your workstreams, and feed requirements, gaps, and improvement ideas back to the software team

 - Support construction, commissioning, and startup in the field, and contribute to Mariana’s program-management standards, templates, and metrics as the portfolio grows



Desired Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field

 - 4+ years of program or project management experience on capital projects in mining, minerals processing, chemical, energy, or heavy-industrial environments

 - Demonstrated ownership of an integrated schedule and budget on a project spanning multiple engineering disciplines and external partners

 - Strong technical fluency—able to read P&IDs, general arrangements, and equipment lists

 - Excellent written and verbal communication and stakeholder management skills,

 - Willingness to travel to project sites as programs require

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Data & Analytics Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.


THE ROLE

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company supplying the minerals critical to modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. Our data systems don't live in a vacuum — they feed process simulators, drive site automation, and are the substrate the business runs its decisions on.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to be the single product owner for the data engineering family — the data platform, analytics, data science, and the AI and agentic workflows built on top of them. Today this work is spread across technical leads and absorbed informally, with no one setting direction across the whole. Your job is to change that: decide what the data organization builds and why, get stakeholders aligned behind it, and make sure engineers can stay heads-down on the work that matters.

This is a hybrid Pioneer/Settler role: you'll get lightweight demos and PoCs built on ambiguous problems, and you'll bring order and cohesive ownership to data work streams that already exist. You'll prioritize ruthlessly and visibly — being explicit about what will not be worked on — and set direction rather than waiting for it to be handed to you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Talk to our internal teams constantly — operators, machine learning engineers, software developers, analysts, and data users are your users, and their problems set the roadmap.

 - Own the roadmap for the data platform, analytics, and data science tooling: what gets built next, for whom, and why.

 - Write the product specs, KPIs, and success metrics that turn ambiguous asks into scoped, shippable work.

 - Own prioritization and stakeholder alignment so engineers stay focused on deep technical work.

 - Make the build-vs-buy calls for BI and analytics, and prioritize tooling that lets stakeholders answer their own questions instead of adding headcount.

 - Own where agents fit versus conventional software, and drive AI and agentic workflows from demo to adopted tool.

 - Decide which new data streams get integrated, when, and to what standard as new sensors and sources come online.

 - Set the bar for what "supported" and "correct" mean as tools graduate from scripts and spreadsheets, and be explicit about what won't be migrated.
   
   


HOW YOU'LL OPERATE

 - Structure from ambiguity: Bring direction to cross-disciplinary initiatives and align stakeholders rather than waiting for direction.

 - Ruthless, visible prioritization: Be explicit about what will not be worked on, not just what will.

 - Hybrid Pioneer/Settler: Get initial prototypes built with stakeholders, then write the roadmap to validate the use case and, if worth it, take it to production.

 - Ecosystem fluency: Understand where Mariana's data sits relative to the systems that consume it and relative to the current frontier of LLM capability, so prioritization calls stay well-calibrated.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Must have

 - 4–8+ years in technical product management, data platform or analytics product roles, or equivalent experience leading cross-disciplinary technical programs

 - Comfortable being the only PM in a highly technical room — you know when to drive a decision, when to defer to engineers, and how to build credibility without being the most technical person there

 - Enough depth in data infrastructure and analytics to earn credibility with data engineers, data scientists, and analysts, and to know when a technical answer is a good one

 - Working fluency with the current LLM/foundation-model landscape and where agentic approaches genuinely fit versus conventional software

 - Track record of bringing structure to ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives: setting direction, aligning stakeholders, and owning outcomes end-to-end

 - Hands-on prototyping ability — you can get a PoC built with stakeholders, not just write requirements for one

 - Strong prioritization and tradeoff skills — you know when to say no, and you say it visibly

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication across audiences, from data engineers to operators to executives

Nice to have

 - Product ownership of a data platform, warehouse, or analytics stack in production

 - Experience with BI/analytics tooling strategy (Hex, Looker, or embedded analytics)

 - Experience shipping LLM-powered or agentic internal tools

 - Background in mining, energy, chemicals, manufacturing, or other heavy industry

 - Experience leading the transition from spreadsheets and scripts to supported software
   
   


WHY THIS ROLE

Most data PM roles hand you a mature warehouse and a dashboard backlog. This role hands you the data platform and analytics layer the business runs on, plus the AI workflows that will increasingly run on top of it, at the moment they move from ad hoc scripts and informal ownership into supported software. At Mariana, you don't need to validate product-market fit, because we are the market: if you identify a real problem and build a real solution, adoption is a conversation, not a sales cycle.


OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, ML & Robotics
jobs.description:

THE ROLE

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company supplying the minerals critical to modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. Our ML systems don't live in a vacuum — they run chemistry and process simulators, see and act in our plants through sensors and robotic systems, and increasingly move toward autonomous industrial process and chemical operations.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to be the single product owner for machine learning and industrial robotics — the ML platform, the simulators it runs, and the perception and robotics initiatives built on it — and to own the seam between our applied AI/ML organization and our software engineering organization. Today this work is split across technical leads with no one setting direction across the whole. Your job is to change that: decide what the ML organization pursues and why, get stakeholders aligned behind it, and make sure engineers can stay heads-down on the work that matters.

Autonomy and robotics here mean industrial: models, perception systems, and robotic hardware that increasingly close the loop on how our plants and chemical processes run.

 - Talk to our internal teams constantly — operators, process engineers, and MLEs are your users, and their problems set the roadmap.

 - Own the roadmap for the ML platform: which capabilities it needs next, for which use cases, and why.

 - Write the product specs, KPIs, and success metrics that turn ambiguous ML and autonomy asks into scoped, shippable work.

 - Own prioritization and stakeholder alignment so MLEs stay focused on deep technical work.

 - Own the path to process autonomy — models that inform, and increasingly set, process and chemical operating decisions — and the simulators that underpin it.

 - Own the roadmap for vision, sensor, and robotics initiatives: which plant problems get a model or a robot first, and what "good enough to deploy" means for each.

 - Own the seam between the applied AI/ML org and the software engineering org, and the boundary with MarianaOS, so nothing falls in the gap.

 - Define what it takes for a model, simulator, or robot to be trusted in production, and be explicit about which initiatives won't be pursued.

 - Hybrid Pioneer/Settler: Prioritize and ship lightweight demos on ambiguous problems while bringing structure to existing work streams that lack cohesive ownership.

 - Ecosystem fluency: Understand the Mariana ML, perception, and robotics ecosystem as a whole — including where it sits relative to the current frontier of model capability — so prioritization calls stay well-calibrated.

Must have

 - 4–8+ years in technical product management, ML platform or robotics product roles, or equivalent experience leading cross-disciplinary technical programs

 - Comfortable being the only PM in a highly technical room — you know when to drive a decision, when to defer to engineers, and how to build credibility without being the most technical person there

 - Enough depth in ML systems — training, evaluation, deployment, perception, simulation — to earn credibility with both ML engineers and software engineers, and to know when a technical answer is a good one

 - Track record of bringing structure to ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives: setting direction, aligning stakeholders, and owning outcomes end-to-end

 - Strong prioritization and tradeoff skills — you know when to say no, and you say it visibly

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication across audiences, from ML engineers to operators to executives

 - Product ownership of an ML platform, MLOps stack, or simulation system in production

 - Prior work on industrial robotics, perception, or closed-loop optimization of chemical or industrial process systems

 - Familiarity with process simulation toolchains (SysCAD or similar)

 - Background in mining, energy, chemicals, manufacturing, or other heavy industry — especially industrial automation or sensor/vision data
